characters.lead: White round-headed 2D stick figure, articulated arms and legs, expressive face, persistent yellow wristband; initially crosses the bridge, notices someone frozen, then turns back.

shots.caption: THE RAIN MADE THE BRIDGE SWAY.
NO ONE SAW THEM TURN BACK.
THEY MOVED AT THE SAME PACE.
THE FAR SIDE WAS CLOSER NOW.
NO ONE HAD TO BE FEARLESS.
NO ONE HAS TO CROSS ALONE.

creative_intent.logline: A confident stick figure crosses a rain-soaked footbridge, notices a blue-scarf stranger frozen at the far end, and turns back. Halfway across together, the bridge shakes and the confident one freezes too; the stranger they helped reaches back first.
creative_intent.hook: A ten-step bridge sways in heavy rain. One figure crosses, then stops when they see another figure unable to take the first step.
creative_intent.theme: Courage is not the absence of fear. Sometimes it is simply choosing to stay beside someone.
creative_intent.emotional_turn: The helper freezes halfway across; the once-frightened companion steadies them, reversing the roles without dialogue.
creative_intent.ending_payoff: Both reach the far side together. The lead looks back and leaves an open hand toward the bridge, suggesting the next person will not have to cross alone.
creative_intent.character_bible: Lead: white round head, small expressive face, articulated thin arms and legs, yellow wristband. Companion: same simple 2D stick-figure rig, slightly smaller, one blue scarf. Preserve silhouettes and accessories in every shot.
creative_intent.environment_bible: One narrow pedestrian bridge with visible rails over a dark river, cold navy/teal storm palette, rain streaks and reflected highlights; city lights behind the bridge; warm dawn at the final beat.
narrative_beats: 0–30s: establish the narrow bridge and rain; the lead crosses, notices the companion frozen at the far end.
30–60s: the lead turns back; other movement continues around them, but they choose to wait rather than pull.
60–90s: the companion takes one step at a time; the lead matches their pace.
90–120s: the bridge shakes; the lead stumbles and freezes, revealing that courage was never effortless.
120–150s: the companion reaches first and steadies the lead; the power dynamic reverses.
150–180s: they continue at one pace and reach the far side together.
180–210s: the rain eases; they pause in the dawn light and leave an open hand toward the next person.

title_alternatives: Walk Beside Me | A Silent Story About Courage
The Bridge Between Us | A 2D Stick Figure Story
Courage Is a Step You Take Together
creative_intent.description: A rain-soaked bridge becomes a test of courage. One figure freezes at the far end, and another turns back instead of rushing them. Halfway across, the bridge shakes—and the person who seemed brave needs help too. A silent 2D stick-figure story about patience, shared courage, and taking the next step together. Original instrumental score and procedural sound effects; no dialogue or voiceover.
growth_hypotheses: A visible hesitation on a narrow bridge in the first five seconds may make the conflict legible without dialogue; validate retention at 0:05.
The helper's return around 0:55 may create a second emotional hook; inspect the 0:45–1:15 retention curve.
The midpoint role reversal may reduce the usual drop after the initial rescue; inspect retention around 1:35–2:05.
The final open-hand image may invite comments about times someone stayed beside the viewer; validate through comments and shares rather than assuming virality.

sources.finding: YouTube reported 6.5 billion microdrama views in H1 2026 and over 50% year-over-year watch-time growth; this is a storytelling-format signal, not a direct forecast for a 210-second 16:9 film.
A third-party weekly motivation Shorts tracker listed action-oriented topics such as talent becoming serious, earned success, and work behind dreams; rankings are not official YouTube analytics.
A third-party stick-figure Shorts ranking showed active recent demand for action-led stick-figure stories and explainers; its sample is limited to the videos returned for its query.

trend_research.conclusion: Use a fast visual conflict and a role-reversal emotional beat; do not copy trend scripts or treat third-party rankings as guaranteed audience demand.

defects.issue: Companion absent in shots 01-10 while captions describe another figure whose feet cannot move; the second character and the emotional conflict are not visually established.
The helper used a fixed translate(360,80) scale(0.70) transform, floating above the bridge deck and overlapping the lead instead of making grounded contact.
Companion disappeared in shots where the lead action was not help/offer, breaking character continuity during the crossing and ending.
The bridge had railings but no visible water or motion, so the caption about the bridge swaying was not sufficiently supported by the background.
